# Select

Displays a list of options for the user to pick from—triggered by a button.

- **Import:** `import { Select, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectScrollDownButton, SelectScrollUpButton, SelectSeparator, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/components-select--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectGroup,
  SelectItem,
  SelectLabel,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
  ThemeProvider,
} from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function SelectExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <Select>
        <SelectTrigger className="w-44" aria-label="Fruit">
          <SelectValue placeholder="Select a fruit" />
        </SelectTrigger>
        <SelectContent>
          <SelectGroup>
            <SelectLabel>Fruits</SelectLabel>
            <SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="banana">Banana</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="blueberry">Blueberry</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="grapes">Grapes</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="pineapple">Pineapple</SelectItem>
          </SelectGroup>
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Select

Its props are `SelectProps`, which is `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof SelectPrimitive.Root> & MixedValueProps`.

- `mixed`: `boolean`, optional.

  The field stands for several values that differ, and shows none.

- `mixedLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Multiple values"`.

  Shown in the empty field, and said with it. Default "Multiple values".

- `onResetMixed`: `() => void`, optional.

  Offer to go back to the several values: drawn under the field while it
  is not `mixed`, and never while it is disabled or read-only.

- `resetMixedLabel`: `string`, optional.

  The reset's words. Default "Reset to multiple values".

- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `open`: `boolean`, optional.
- `defaultOpen`: `boolean`, optional.
- `onOpenChange`: `(open: boolean) => void`, optional.
- `dir`: `Direction`, optional.
- `name`: `string`, optional.
- `autoComplete`: `string`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional.
- `required`: `boolean`, optional.
- `form`: `string`, optional.
- `value`: `string`, optional.
- `defaultValue`: `string`, optional.
- `onValueChange`: `(value: string) => void`, optional.

## SelectItem

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `SelectItemProps`, which extends `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof SelectPrimitive.Item>`.

- `count`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.

  A count beside the option's words (GAP-164), as a neutral Counter at the
  row's end, before the check's place. It sits outside the item text, so
  the closed select shows the words alone. A number is written in the
  app's grouping (the document's `lang`, as Calendar reads it: "1,234",
  "1.234" in German), and the option is named by its words, then its
  count: "POI, 96". A caller's own `aria-label` wins.

- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional.
- `value`: `string`, **required**.
- `textValue`: `string`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).
